name: Prize crossword No 24,409
preamble: Eight clues contain no definition; their answers are of a kind.

clue.text: Symbols of love awards one had to enter

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: trophies handed out as prizes
I'd is the contraction of 'I had', with I standing for one

explanation.surface: Someone had to go up and collect awards shaped like love tokens, perhaps at a Valentine's ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One had' must be read as the contraction 'I'd', with the Roman-numeral sense of one as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid, the Roman god with bow and arrows, is the conventional emblem of romantic attraction on cards and decorations.

clue.text: Function after short contest

blocks.note: comp is the clipped form of competition
to act is to function or operate

explanation.surface: An event held straight after a brief competition, such as a prize-giving.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the eight clues with no definition: a compact is a kind of camera, the theme the preamble hints at. 'After' puts the function second.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is a small point-and-shoot camera type, one of the themed photographic devices in this grid.

clue.text: Tragic poet losing home (English)

indicators.note: losing one thing while the bracketed item comes in, so a letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: Sylvia Plath, the American poet who took her own life
H is the abbreviation for home, as in football results
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A doomed poet loses their English home.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition here: a plate camera is one of the theme's kinds of camera. Plath's H gives way to E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate camera, using glass photographic plates, is an early type of camera and belongs to the themed set.

clue.text: Appreciate computing and stuff? A life initially is needed!

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
IT, information technology, covers computing and the like
taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone urges a love of computers on us: what you need is a life!
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: a digital camera is one of the theme's camera kinds. To 'dig' is 1960s slang for appreciate.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital camera records images electronically rather than on film, and is one of the themed camera types.

clue.text: Short warrant officer covered in hair cleaner

indicators.note: something covered in a layer sits inside it, so one piece is wrapped by another

blocks.note: a mop is a thick untidy head of hair
RSM, short for Regimental Sergeant Major, a British Army warrant officer

explanation.surface: A small army officer smothered in shampoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair cleaner' reads as shampoo, but the hair is the outer piece and 'cleaner' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Mop is a British jocular name for a charwoman, a woman employed to clean houses or offices.

clue.text: See 22
Electric supply energy stored in the switching, which facilitates a nautical manoeuvre

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something which facilitates', the noun

indicators.note: what is stored sits inside its store, so a letter goes inside a word
switching things around changes their order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the mains is the domestic electricity supply
E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A technical note about wiring that somehow helps a ship change course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electric supply' and 'switching' keep the surface in a power plant; the sailing sense only arrives in the final words.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing boat the mainsheet is the rope that controls the mainsail, used when tacking, gybing or trimming.

clue.text: Leg space

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs
a hole is an empty space or gap

explanation.walkthrough: No definition: a pinhole camera is one of the theme's camera kinds. The two words look like 'legroom' but each supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinhole camera uses a tiny aperture instead of a lens, the simplest of the themed camera types.

clue.text: Revolutionary street entertainers in rags circling Miller

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all the way around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: rags and organs are both words for newspapers or periodicals
a miller is one who grinds grain

explanation.surface: Ragged revolutionary buskers surrounding a man called Miller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' is part of the definition, a joke on turning the handle; 'in rags' tempts as an anagram, but rags are newspapers, as are organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ-grinders played barrel organs in the street by cranking a handle round and round, hence revolutionary.

clue.text: Book about Hammer lacking start and finish

indicators.note: without its beginning and end, a word keeps only its inner letters
about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the word minus its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A book about a hammer that has neither beginning nor end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the subject of', but it turns the trimmed letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's novel, so the title stands for a particular work of literature.

clue.text: Bird some say Fielding reproduced with two rooks

indicators.note: reproduced means made again, here remade in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A bird that some claim the novelist Fielding bred, along with a couple of rooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird, rooks and breeding make a birdwatching picture, but 'bird' is British slang, which is why 'some say' qualifies it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a man's bird is his female partner, a usage only certain speakers would use.

clue.text: Primitive form of expression not right for rider

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is dropped

blocks.note: cave art, the paintings of prehistoric people
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An early style of communication unsuited to a horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horseman, but in law it is an added condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to a document; a caveat is a warning or qualification attached to a statement.

clue.text: Strong dislike, though there are other interpretations?

definitions.note: read as 'a version', two words, a phrase rather than a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: deep distaste
second meaning, split in two: just one reading among several

explanation.surface: Someone hates something intensely, while conceding that others might see it differently.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the word must be split into an article and a noun for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is a firm antipathy; split, the letters say one possible account among many others.

clue.text: Gloomy yet stirring wordy history

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dark yet rousing account told at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wordy' looks like long-winded, but it means 'of words'.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymology traces the origins and development of individual words through time, the life story of vocabulary.

clue.text: Two centuries since one in battle footwear

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
Roman numeral
the Battle of Mons, 1914, in Belgium

explanation.surface: Two hundred years after one wore particular shoes in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Mons was the British Expeditionary Force's first action of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Moccasins are soft leather slip-on shoes, originally worn by Native Americans, a type of footwear.

clue.text: One of many passed on by Mother Kelly?

definitions.text: One of many passed on by Mother

blocks.clueFragment: One of many passed on by Mother
blocks.note: first meaning: a unit of heredity inherited from a parent
second meaning: first name of the dancer Kelly, star of Singin' in the Rain

explanation.surface: Something handed down by an Irish mother, as in the old music-hall song Mother Kelly's Doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother Kelly' reads as one person, but the clue splits there; the question mark marks Kelly as an example of a bearer of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents pass on thousands of hereditary units to a child; and the Hollywood dancer was called this.

clue.text: Be retrogressive as a player

definitions.note: 'as a player' introduces the noun, a defensive player

blocks.note: first meaning: to go backwards
second meaning: a defender in football or hockey

explanation.surface: An actor slips back into old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests an actor; here it is a team position.
explanation.definitionFit: To back is to move in reverse; a full-back or half-back is a defensive position in team sports.

clue.text: Before 1 PM and a quarter

blocks.note: Gordon Brown, British Prime Minister 2007 to 2010
the digit read as the letter it resembles
east, one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A time just before 1.15 in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: the Brownie was Kodak's famous box camera. '1 PM' and 'a quarter' read as a time, but PM is the Prime Minister, placed before the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodak Brownie was a cheap box camera that made snapshot photography popular, one of the themed cameras.

clue.text: Car taken by one time British rock star

blocks.note: the Mini, the classic small British car
a means one
standard abbreviation
Midge Ure, Scottish musician of Ultravox

explanation.surface: A vehicle once driven by a famous British rock musician.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: a miniature camera is one of the theme's kinds. 'One time' reads as former, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniature cameras, such as the Minox, take very small film formats, and are one of the themed types.

clue.text: No outdoor type's pub drink, by the sound of it

definitions.note: jocular: one who is in, not out

indicators.note: judged by how it sounds, not how it is written, so speech matters here

blocks.note: an inn is a pub, and cider is a drink served there

explanation.surface: A homebody's favourite tipple at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on 'type's' belongs to the surface; the pub supplies the possessive in the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is literally one on the inside, a whimsical opposite of someone who loves the outdoors.

clue.text: Decisions that result in lined paper?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun 'things that result in lined paper'

blocks.note: first meaning: official judgments by a court or authority
second meaning: the ruled lines drawn across a page

explanation.surface: Judgments that leave a lot of paperwork in their wake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense is a playful stretch: paper is ruled with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's pronouncements are rulings; drawing parallel lines across a sheet with a ruler is also ruling it.

clue.text: Stop - just gin, no vermouth!

blocks.note: first meaning: wait, don't move
second meaning: a barman's order to leave out the Italian vermouth from a gin and it

explanation.surface: A drinker cries halt: plain gin, please, and keep the vermouth away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin and it' is a British drink of gin and Italian vermouth, 'it' short for Italian; to 'hold' an item is to leave it out of an order.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a command to halt, and a request to omit the Italian vermouth from the drink.

clue.text: Shell protecting the effeminate French ruler?

indicators.note: something that protects surrounds and shields, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a pod is the shell of peas or beans
la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: An armour guarding a rather unmanly French king.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: the Polaroid is the instant camera of the theme. 'Effeminate' asks for the French feminine article, which nonsensically pairs with a masculine king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polaroid instant camera produced a developed print within minutes, one of the themed camera types.

clue.text: Recording Leonard's unconscious

blocks.note: a single is a record of one song
Len is short for Leonard, so Len's
a reflex is an involuntary, unthinking reaction

explanation.surface: A tape of someone called Leonard while he is out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: the single lens reflex, or SLR, is one of the theme's cameras. 'Unconscious' is taken as an adjective for automatic action.
explanation.definitionFit: A single lens reflex camera uses a mirror so the photographer views through the taking lens, a themed camera type.

clue.text: Material is short and only to be ordered

indicators.note: being short means cut down, so a word loses letters
putting things in order means arranging them anew

blocks.note: 'n' is the clipped form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fabric in short supply that can only be got by placing an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is short' reads as scarce, but it cuts 'and' down to its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer fabric, used for stockings and clothing, so a kind of material.

clue.text: Hundred and nine, name forgotten, rambling and left alone

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so a letter goes missing
rambling wanders all over, so letters stray out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An old person of 109, forgetting names, wandering about and left to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: One N is removed from the two number words before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unhindered means free of obstruction or interference, the state of someone left to get on with things.

clue.text: See 22
Substitute, er, rested, with a bit of a snore

blocks.note: taken as written
sat means stayed seated, resting
a snore is written zzz in comics, so one z is a bit of it

explanation.surface: A replacement player hesitates, sits down and nods off a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Cartoon snoring is drawn as a row of Zs, so one Z is a fragment of a snore.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz, borrowed from German, describes an inferior imitation used in place of the real thing.

clue.text: World star, a sport, making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way one came, so the sequence runs backwards

blocks.note: the Sun is our star
taken as written
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A global sporting star staging a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'World star' reads as an international celebrity, but World is the definition and the star our Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus, the seventh planet from the Sun, is a world in the astronomical sense of a planetary body.
